subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Wedge: A Moving Inclined Plane
description: A 60-second lesson on The Wedge: A Moving Inclined Plane.

hook.text: An axe splits a log in one swing. The blade barely touches the wood — so where does the force come from?

buildup.text: A wedge is two inclined planes joined back to back. It converts downward force into sideways push.

discovery.text: The thinner the wedge, the greater the force multiplication. A razor blade is an extreme wedge.

twist.text: Your front teeth are wedges. So are nails, chisels, and ship bows cutting through water.

climax.text: Without the wedge, we couldn't cut, split, or pierce anything. Civilization depends on it.

punchline.text: The wedge turns a push into a split. Simple geometry, huge results.

quiz.question: How does a wedge multiply force?
options: It stores energy in its material and releases it on impact
It converts a downward push into a much larger sideways force
It reduces friction between surfaces through its smooth shape
